H.why: Analyst headlines describe Ethernet extending its lead in AI back-end networks.

T.why: Operator-documented production across generations; 800G dominates back-end shipments.

A.why: About two-thirds of AI-cluster switch sales in Q1 2026; back-end passed front-end in Q2.

Q.why: Arista 10-Q to 30 Sep 2026: remaining performance obligations about $8.6B (91% to be recognised within two years) and deferred revenue $6,839.5M, both contractual buyer-side balances; 100+ Etherlink customers; buyers fund from cash flow and investment-grade debt. Its $11.4B of non-cancellable purchase commitments are owed to its own suppliers, so they show vendor confidence, not buyer commitment. Customer-concentration percentages were not read at origin.

E.why: Operators report reliability outcomes; no matched-baseline cost or energy result is public.

milestone.text: 1.6T systems: trials in 2H 2026, production deployment expected 2027 (Arista).

H.why: Framed as the fabric losing share to Ethernet.

T.why: 800G systems shipping in volume with the Blackwell Ultra platform.

A.why: Sales more than tripled in Q1 2026; about one-third of AI-cluster switch sales.

Q.why: Single vendor. NVIDIA's 10-Q confirms three direct customers at 16%, 15% and 13% (44%) of first-half FY2027 revenue; it holds large stakes in and guarantees for customers.

E.why: Meta ran matched 24,576-GPU clusters on RoCE and on InfiniBand and reports both ran without network bottlenecks: parity, not a benefit.

milestone.text: 800G ramp arrived with the platform it was tied to.

H.why: Products marketed as UEC-compliant; the specification is described in the present tense.

T.why: Specification 1.0 (June 2025), then 1.0.1 and 1.0.2 correcting congestion-control algorithms, 1.0.3 (July 2026, adds 200 Gb/s per lane) and 1.1 (12 Oct 2026, 764 pages, adds a scale-up profile); Section 8 of the specification states compliance is self-attested from UEC checklists; the 562-page specification's own overview paper (spec authors from AMD, Broadcom, HPE, Microsoft, OpenAI, Cisco, Intel) reports no measurements and calls the first products future; compliance is self-attested, with no test lab or plugfest result published. The UEC Transport and PHY/link-layer profile matrices and compliance checklists (revision 1.0) define what a compliance claim covers, and the June 2025 test-bed recommendations (revision 1.0, marked UEC proprietary and confidential) put interoperation, system and performance testing out of scope; none of them is a test result.

A.why: Oracle states it will be first to deploy UEC-capable NICs: an intent in the future tense, with no port or cluster counts and no proof the UET protocol itself is in production.

Q.why: No UET-specific revenue, backlog or design win on the AMD or Broadcom calls of August to November 2026; a strict reading gives 1.

E.why: Vendor claim only: 25% better RDMA performance than RoCEv2, workload and baseline unstated.

milestone.text: UEC-compliant 800G NICs ship inside AMD Helios racks ramping in Q4 2026.

H.why: Described as the dominant scale-up fabric today, with open alternatives expected to challenge it.

T.why: Dominates scale-up deployments across successive accelerator generations.

A.why: Analysts describe it as dominating scale-up deployments.

Q.why: Single vendor. NVIDIA's 10-Q confirms three direct customers at 16%, 15% and 13% (44%) of first-half FY2027 revenue; large stakes in and guarantees for customers. Networking is not reported apart from compute, so NVLink revenue is not separable in the filing.

E.why: No NVLink revenue or price disclosed; cost is bundled into rack-scale systems. Best proxy is a trade-press estimate.

milestone.text: Next generation arrives with the 2026 accelerator platform; no dated event adds buyer-economics evidence.

H.why: Positioned as the open alternative to NVLink; a 2.0 specification followed in April 2026.

T.why: Targets rest on simulation; a hardware teardown finds first racks carrying UALink over Ethernet because native switch chips were not ready; no sampling statement found by 11 Nov 2026.

A.why: No native UALink switch in products; first AMD Helios racks use UALink over Ethernet instead.

Q.why: Venture and acquisition capital only: a $200M Series A and a $540M acquisition; no recognized product revenue found. Astera Labs, a named UALink supplier, reports Q3 2026 revenue of $584.9M led by Scorpio switches but names UALink only in its portfolio description and, among its forward-looking risks, the timing of any initial UALink 2.0 programs; no UALink revenue is disclosed.

E.why: Developer targets only; no buyer-stated or matched figure for a native fabric.

milestone.text: First merchant switch silicon samples at end of 2026, volume in 2027. First racks shipped without it.

eth_scaleup.name: Ethernet scale-up
eth_scaleup.sub: UALink over Ethernet, RoCE; not yet ESUN

H.why: Vendor and operator roadmaps present Ethernet as the open scale-up answer; Arista announced an ESUN-based rack architecture on 3 Nov 2026 (an announcement, not a shipment).

T.why: Meta's own post (12 Oct 2026) says its Tahan Ethernet scale-up switch for MTIA 300 is shipping: Broadcom Tomahawk 5, RoCE transport, four switches per 16 accelerators, 6.4 Tb/s per accelerator. No unit counts, and it is Meta's own variant, not ESUN. AMD separately reports first Helios revenue shipments (Q3 2026); a teardown shows UALink over Ethernet on Tomahawk 6.

A.why: Meta reports Ethernet scale-up in production for its own accelerator; analysts see scale-up only emerging in 2H 2026.

Q.why: AMD's 8-K of 24 Feb 2026 (read at origin) states Meta agreed a binding commitment to buy the initial 1 GW of Instinct GPU products, no period stated; the 6 GW total is not stated as binding. Meta's warrant covers up to 160M shares at $0.01 (first tranche on shipment of the initial 1 GW; price thresholds escalating to $600). The 10-Q to 26 Sep 2026 reports no warrant shares vested, a $1.1B warrant-liability charge in Q3 and $4.5B of unrecognised grant-date value. AMD's 8-K for 5 Oct 2025 shows the same structure with OpenAI (binding initial 1 GW of MI450, a 160M-share warrant at $0.01, 6 GW for full vesting, price targets to $600). The commitments are for GPUs, not the scale-up fabric, and supplier equity sits beside the orders, so Q stays 2.

E.why: Vendor simulation only (33% switching cost saving, 13% training speed-up), and the saving is tied to scale-out switches.

milestone.text: AMD Helios racks with UALink-over-Ethernet on Broadcom silicon: shipments from late Q3 2026, ramp in Q4.

H.why: Positioned by vendors as core AI-factory infrastructure.

T.why: Oracle describes a SmartNIC offload device in production compute shapes but gives no counts and does not name the silicon; a strict merchant-only reading gives 2.

A.why: Two cloud providers took most shipments in 2024; in late 2026 analysts still ask whether adoption will broaden beyond established cloud deployments.

Q.why: NVIDIA reports networking as one line ($31.4B, fiscal 2026) with no DPU breakout; trackers describe hyperscalers on customised devices.

E.why: Google's Wave (ASPLOS 2025) reports against on-host baselines on a co-designed Intel IPU: 1.1% to 7.4% slowdown, 16 host cores saved (memory management), 8 cores (RPC), 11.2% VM gain. A research system, not a merchant DPU in production; an independent lab study (S112) finds 7.5x lower compute throughput than the host. No cost figure.

milestone.text: Next-generation merchant DPU launches with 2026 accelerator platforms; it does not address the missing economics evidence.

H.why: Described as moving from long-promised to entering production.

T.why: Meta ran 15 CPO switches for nine months (36 million device-hours) after one million flap-free port-hours in lab testing.

A.why: Early deployments in 2026; unit volumes still small.

Q.why: Early revenue plus strategic capital upstream: NVIDIA put $2B each into two laser suppliers with supply agreements.

E.why: Buyer tests report about 65% lower optics power and fewer interruptions (0.2% against 1.22% a year) than pluggables.

milestone.text: 102.4T CPO platforms enter production in 2027; 2026 initial deployments arrived when analysts forecast in 2025.

H.why: Less prominent than co-packaged optics in coverage.

T.why: Meta's OCP 2026 talk (slides read in full): live production on one hop of a DSF fabric (4k modules, 4 months) shows about 2x fewer interruptions and about 2.6x fewer service-affecting failures than retimed optics at the same link mode; a ~1k-module lab loopback logged 0 module-attributable failures in 2.96M link-hours. 100G/lane only; Meta's own measurement, no independent replication.

A.why: Meta states a limited LPO-LPO deployment: about 4k modules on one network hop for 4 months, the rest of the fabric retimed. Oracle production is reported only in a secondary write-up (S39). Scale is small against a hyperscale fleet.

Q.why: A chip supplier reports LPO revenue growing inside a $71.6M data-centre line; no filing separates LPO revenue or units.

E.why: Meta's lab, fan speed fixed: -46% power per module and -17.5 C module temperature; fewer interruptions in production. No cost-per-bit or fleet energy result is public.

milestone.text: No dated milestone admitted that would add economics evidence.

T.why: Meta presented its large-scale deployment of 800G active electrical cables in AI data centres at OCP 2026; failure-rate data inside the talk is unread.

A.why: Meta, a named buyer, describes 800G AEC in its fleet with three qualified suppliers; Credo's 10-Q reports revenue of $479.0M in the quarter to 1 Aug 2026, with over 90% of the increase from AEC shipments to hyperscale customers.

Q.why: Recognized revenue, but concentrated: the 10-K for the year to 2 May 2026 shows Customer A at 49% and Customer B at 32% of revenue (81% together), receivables at 53%, 20% and 19% for three customers, top ten about 90% of revenue; the quarter to May 2026 had a top three of 77% on the call. The 10-Q for the quarter to 1 Aug 2026 shows Customer A at 43% and Customer B at 28% of revenue (71%), receivables at 57% and 28%, and $222.2M of non-cancellable purchase commitments owed by Credo to its own suppliers; no buyer commitments are disclosed.

E.why: Vendor financials and a bounded vendor comparison; the only buyer statement is qualitative.

milestone.text: No dated milestone admitted that would add economics evidence.

power.name: Site power and grid
power.why: Average grid-connection wait above four years in primary US markets; transformer lead times above 160 weeks; Microsoft built less than guided because capacity arrived late.

packaging.name: Advanced packaging
packaging.why: CoWoS supply about 20% short of demand in mid-2026, expected to narrow to about 10% by year end; capacity concentrated in Taiwan.

memory.name: High-bandwidth memory
memory.why: One supplier's HBM4 volume ramp moved to Q3 2026 and the 2026 shipment outlook was cut from 4.5 to 4.0 billion gigabits.

lasers.name: Indium phosphide lasers
lasers.why: A leading supplier ships about 30% below demand with capacity committed through 2027; refined indium supply is concentrated in China and under export control.

policy.name: Export policy
policy.why: Since 15 January 2026, certain AI chips for China are licensed case by case with conditions, alongside a 25% tariff proclamation. The rules also changed in January 2025 and May 2025.

taiwan.name: Taiwan supply disruption
taiwan.note: Advanced packaging is concentrated in Taiwan, so every accelerator-dependent category is blocked.

indium.name: Indium export halt
indium.note: Optical categories are blocked; copper categories are not.

export.name: Export rules tightened
export.note: Binding for sales into restricted destinations; shown here as binding for all.

grid.name: Grid delays worsen
grid.note: No new capacity can be energized on schedule, whatever the fabric.
